Someone in front of you is driving 3-5 mph slower than you are and you want to pass. You get over into the passing lane, and surprise surprise, there's another car driving slower than you about two car lengths ahead. As a driver that lives in the "country" (where most roads are 2-4 lanes total), city driving scares the hell out of me largely because of the (lack of) signs. Whenever I drive in larger cities I always feel like the roads are designed for locals and have little regard for new people to the city. Important notices won't have a sign until it's right next to the spot that you need to make a decision (so if you didn't know you had to take action until you saw the sign, you're fucked because it's too late to act now), some places don't even have signs at all. Stoplights and lane changes are especially problematic for me. City to city (sometimes even within the same city) they differ with which lanes are right only, left only, and straight. One light might have four lanes: left only, left/straight, straight, and right/straight. Another might be left only, left/straight, right only, right only. So, going left or straight are usually simple enough (just go to the furthest lane for each), but the straight lane is a confusing gamble (you try to stay in one of the center lanes, but it might actually be the other center lane that's straight). Further, there are some cities near me that don't even have any signs on the side of the road which say which lane is which at the stoplight; instead, there's only painted arrows on the road, so you have no way of knowing what direction your lane is going (since the cars will be covering the line anyway). Even for the stoplights that do have signs, unless you're on the far right lane there's no way you can see them unless you're in a tall vehicle since the other cars will be in the way, and further (as mentioned before) the signs don't appear until you're right at the stoplight so you don't have enough time to react.
